correctness.rationale: The exact affine map \(F(y)=1+(1-2^{-q})y\) and binary precision grids \(p\) and \(p+r\) give an increasing finite-state chain. For \(r<q\), its first accessible absorbing state is \(B=2^q-(2^{q-r}-1)2^{q-p}\); the monotone map prevents bypassing \(B\). For \(r\ge q\), every state below the exact limit has positive upward probability. These yield almost-sure absorption in finite time and finite expected absorption time. The exact last-step probability is \(2^{-r}\) below the threshold or \(2^{-q}\) above it. A standalone rational checker enumerated 224 complete reachable finite-state transition graphs and tested these algebraic facts; finite checks are not substituted for an infinite proof.

This is a mathematically motivated stability/quantization cutoff rather than a generic exercise or table recomputation.
